query: What open-response signals predict low learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: teacher_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Teacher responsiveness/feedback quality extracted from the open response is a distinct construct from satisfaction rating, plausibly drives satisfaction, and is knowable independently of the rating. Legitimate predictor without restating or leaking the focus.

per_column.name: instructional_mode_quality
per_column.rationale: Characterizes the delivery format (interactive vs passive/worksheet-only). This is a plausible antecedent of learning satisfaction and lies outside the focus variable, so it carries genuine predictive signal.

per_column.name: student_engagement_signal
per_column.rationale: Engagement (active vs disengaged/avoidance) is a separate behavioral signal correlated with but not a restatement of satisfaction. Some risk it co-moves closely with satisfaction, but it is a distinct variable, not a deterministic function or component of the rating, so it qualifies as a predictor.

per_column.name: subject_format_fit
per_column.rationale: How well the subject adapts to the format is an external situational feature plausibly influencing satisfaction; not a restatement or leakage of the rating.

per_column.name: peer_interaction_loss
per_column.rationale: Degree of peer/community loss mentioned is a distinct affective/social factor that plausibly predicts lower satisfaction, and is knowable from the response independently of the numeric rating.

judge.rationale: All five added columns are semantically extracted latent constructs from the open response that lie outside the satisfaction rating itself — none restate, decompose, or leak the focus variable. They span complementary explanatory dimensions (teaching quality, delivery mode, engagement, subject-format fit, social loss), giving a model substantial and diverse predictive leverage beyond the original metadata columns. Slight discount because engagement and satisfaction may be tightly coupled and some categories are sparse, but as a set these are strong, non-mechanical predictors.
